rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A general repetition rule says a repeated definite noun denotes the same referent, while repeated indefinite wording can denote another; on this reading the second ease differs from the first but the hardship is the same.
rows.anchor: في أنها إن أعيدت معرفة كان الثاني هو الأول , وإن أعيدت نكرة كان غيره

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains the indefinite ease as a portion of the whole; a fresh statement can therefore mean a different portion without difficulty.
rows.anchor: وقال في الكشاف : وأما اليسر فمنكر متناول لبعض الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finishing the present ease may mean relief from jihad that is followed by another demanding duty, especially when people enter Islam in multitudes.
rows.anchor: من جهادك الذي أنت فيه في وقت المخاطبة بهذا الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The completed task may instead be the weighty worship of receiving and bearing revelation, after which another duty remains.
rows.anchor: أو من العبادة الثقيلة العظيمة بسماع الوحي وتحمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When one task is complete, the command is to labor in another act of worship, such as glorification, seeking forgiveness, or voluntary devotion.
rows.anchor: أي بالغ في التعب بعبادة أخرى من التسبيح والاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant should direct hope and petition to the Lord alone, since He alone has power and gives creatures whatever power they possess.
rows.anchor: أي بالسؤال لأنه القادر وحده كما قدر على تربيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's ending connects to its opening as an effect to its cause, and the next surah is fitted to this ending.
rows.anchor: فقد اتصل هذا الآخر بالأول اتصال المعلول بالعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending points to renewed devotion after the Prophet finishes the Arab campaign, corresponding to eight years after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: بعد انقضاء ما يوازي عدد آي هذه السورة من السنين بعد الهجرة , وهي ثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aspiring to the better hereafter also hints at the approaching end of life, as signaled by Sūrat al-Naṣr.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى قرب الأجل بما أشارت إليه سورة النصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose is to command its specially favored addressee to worship the Creator and Commander, thanking Him, avoiding ingratitude, hoping for Paradise, and fearing Hell in view of judgment.
rows.anchor: الأمر لا سيما للمقصود بالتفضيل في سورة التين بعبادة من له الخلق والأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Iqraʾ signals the command to worship and, by implication, salvation at the final judgment; al-ʿAlaq signals creation and the beginning and end of human life.
rows.anchor: على أن ' اقرأ ' يشير إلى الأمر ، ' والعلق ' يشير غلى الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who knows he was created from clinging blood can infer that his Creator can resurrect him from dust, which is more receptive to life than blood; belief in resurrection should prompt action.
rows.anchor: فإن التراب أقبل للحياة من الدم ، ومن صدق بالإعادة عمل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clinging substance is singled out as the carrier of life, which is why it is called a soul.
rows.anchor: وخص العلق لأنه مركب الحياة ، ولذلك سمي نفسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God as perfect and uniquely divine, universally merciful and deserving of gratitude, and specially merciful in granting chosen servants noble gifts.
rows.anchor: الذي عمت نعمته فاستوج بالشكر من سائر البرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah follows al-Ḍuḥā and al-Sharḥ, which recall divine favors and end by directing hope to God, and al-Tīn, which establishes His power and hence resurrection; listeners are thus led to ask how to secure a good judgment.
rows.anchor: لما أمره سبحانه وتعالى في الضحى بالتحديث بنعمته , وذكره بمجامعها في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah answers by beginning with knowledge of human creation and stages, including admirable and blameworthy states, as signs of God's power and favor.
rows.anchor: بالتعريف بالعلم الأصل ذاكرا أصل منخلقه سبحانه وتعالى في أحسن تقويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active verb is placed before its prepositional phrase because this is more forceful, especially in the first revelation, where the command to read is paramount.
rows.anchor: وقدم الفعل العامل في الجار والمجرور هنا لأنه أوقع في النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting the object of “read” signals that the reading is the comprehensive Qur'an, containing every good; God alone enables the Prophet to read it.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى : أوجد القراءة لما لا مقروء غيره , وهو القرآن الجامع لكل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the name of your Lord” means beginning with the basmala, seeking the benefactor's aid, or mentioning His name; in the last reading, the name stands for His exalted attributes.
rows.anchor: حال كونك مفتتحا القراءة { باسم ربك } أي بأن تبسمل , أو مستعينا

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say recitation is not complete without naming God; naming Him honors both the name and its bearer and all His attributes.
rows.anchor: قالوا : وهذا يدل على أن القراءة لا تكون تامة غلا بالتسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's nurturing attribute, rather than the encompassing divine name, comforts the Prophet and recalls the favors recalled in al-Sharḥ; the command came when he loved retreat for worship in Ḥirāʾ.
rows.anchor: وتأنيسا له صلى الله عليه وسلم لكونه أول ما نزل حين حبب إليه الخلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel brought the first five verses of the surah to the Prophet; the opening echoes the basmala through divine attributes, creation, generosity, and teaching.
rows.anchor: وفجاءه جبرائيل عليه الصلاة والسلام بخمس آيات من أول هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order to read the Qur'an also alludes to seeking refuge from devils when reciting.
rows.anchor: وأشار إلى الاستعاذة بالأمر بالقرآن لما أفهمه قوله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited commands to seek refuge and the protective veil apply against human and jinn devils when reading the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أي الشياطين الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is placed before command because it is visible, easier to understand, and a clear proof of existence, power, and wisdom; knowing God through His acts is the first obligation.
rows.anchor: وبدأ بالخلق لأنه محسوس بالعين , فهو أعلق بالفهم , وأقرب إلى التصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unexpressed object of “created” makes the attribute comprehensive: everything that comes into existence is God's making and remains subject to His permission, prevention, harm, or benefit.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعوله إشارة إلى أنه له هذا الوصف وهو التقدير والإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is singled out because humans are the highest animals and a concentrated summary of creation, making their creation an especially clear proof of the Maker and the duty to worship Him alone.
rows.anchor: وكان الإنسان أكمل الحيوان وزبدة مخضه , ولباب حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word al-ʿalaq denotes thick, deep-red clotted blood and can also denote sticky clay; Arabs acknowledged both as origins of human creation.
rows.anchor: أي خلق هذا النوع من هذا الشيء وهو دم شديد الحمرة جامد غليظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blood is the source and carrier of life, and the verse presents creation through causes even though God can create without a causal sequence; the author also says eating blood imparts its qualities.
rows.anchor: لأنه أصل الإنسان وغيره من الحيوان وهو مركب الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared word al-ʿalaq supports the Shāfiʿī proof for using a homonym with both meanings at once; its breadth may encompass clay as well as blood.
rows.anchor: فالآية من أدلة إمامنا الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه على استعمال المشترك في معنييه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implies that blood and earth are unlawful as food in their original states but become lawful after transformation; reddish semen is not transformed, while blood turned to flesh and earth mixed with water into grain or dates are transformed.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى حرمة أكل ما هو أصلنا من الدم والتراب قبل أن يستحيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge about denying judgment cannot literally accuse the Prophet, whom God has protected from denial; it addresses his community, as in the conditional warning elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وحكم هذا القبيل واضح في حق من تعدىة إليه الخطاب وقصد بالحقيقة به من أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended question asks what could make people hesitate about judgment after clear evidence, and whether a wise God would create differing human states in the best form without purpose.
rows.anchor: أفيليق به وهو العليم الخبير أن يجعل اختلاف أحوالكم في الشكوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is the healing, clarifying guide to humanity's beginning and end, so the command is to read it reflectively; its description as guidance and mercy reinforces this role.
rows.anchor: وهو كتابه المبين , الذي جعله الله تعالى تبيانا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity was created in the best form and then reduced to the lowest, producing opposing outcomes by God's prior wisdom and will; He could have guided every soul if He willed.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فإنه تعالى أعلم عباده بخلقه الإنسان في أحسن تقويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding surahs show the highest outcome for the noblest human, the Prophet, including God's promise that He will give him until he is content.
rows.anchor: حال نبينا المصطفى صلى الله عليه وسلم وجليل وعده الكريم له في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah contrasts the Prophet's exalted station, promised in the previous surahs, with the opposing human state described from the one who forbids a servant's prayer; canonical surah order is not chronological revelation order.
rows.anchor: فوقع تعقيب - ذلك بسورة تضمنت الإشارة إلى حال من جعل في الظرف الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection that al-ʿAlaq was among the first revelations misunderstands the arrangement: surah order follows the Prophet's arrangement or the Companions' judgment, not revelation chronology.
rows.anchor: ترتيب السور ما هي عليه راجع إلى فعله عليه الصلاة والسلام أكان ذلك بتوقيف منه أو باجتهاد الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “Read” emphasizes the command, comforts the Prophet, and distinguishes the One who brings revelation from the false objects of worship; the Prophet had said he could not read.
rows.anchor: مكررا للأمر بالقراءة تنبيها على عظم شأنها وتأنيسا له صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being al-Akram means absolute perfection in essence, attributes, and acts, free of every deficiency, and the source of gifts beyond measure.
rows.anchor: الذي له الكمال الأعظم مطلقا من جهة الذات ومن جهة الصفات ومن جهة الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the Prophet was unlettered, God's generosity grants his community knowledge and honor beyond prior communities despite their shorter lives, through teaching and divine bestowal.
rows.anchor: يفيض على أمته الأمية من العلم والحظ ما لم يفضه على أمة قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing has benefits beyond comprehension and supports the ordering of worldly and religious life, in this life and the next, displaying God's subtle wisdom and governance.
rows.anchor: لأنها انبنت عليها استقامة أمور الدنيا والدين في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches necessary and theoretical knowledge, including scripture, religious practice, transactions, and crafts, while also giving uncaused insight into reasoning, conclusions, and intuitive truths.
rows.anchor: أي الذي من شأنه الأنس بما هو فيه لا ينتقل إلى غيره بل ينساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If learning came only through ordinary causes, people would be equal in teaching time and basic knowledge as they are in gestation and humanity; divine bestowal accounts for their differences.
rows.anchor: ولو كان ذلك بالأسباب فقط لتساوى الناس في مدة التعليم وفي أصل المعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By showing humanity's origin and movement from a low state to a high one, God establishes His lordship and generosity; the passage hints at the worlds of creation and command.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر سبحانه مبدأ الإنسان ومنتهاه بنقله من أخس الحالات إلى أعلاها

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Malwī argues that if anything were nobler than knowledge among gifts, it would have been named after God's description as the Most Generous; the author draws from this the honor of teaching scholars.
rows.anchor: قال الملوي : ولو كان شيء من العطاء والنعم أشرف من العلم لذكره عقب صفة الأكرمية

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī remarks that each of the two worlds, creation and command, has both a particular and a universal aspect.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي , وفي كل من العالمين خصوص وعموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches the unlettered Prophet, making him more learned than those who write and raising him above every lofty station.
rows.anchor: فتكون أنت - بما أشارت إليه صفة الأكرمية على ما أنت فيه من الأمية - أعلم من أهل الأقلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most humans, except those God protects, transgress when they perceive themselves as wealthy; self-sufficiency blinds them to continuing need and makes them exceed proper limits.
rows.anchor: أن يزيد على الحد الذي لا ينبغي له مجاوزته كما يزيد الخلط الدموي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing oneself as self-sufficient means inwardly recognizing one's own wealth; this is the dominant human tendency and changes conduct toward whatever one no longer needs.
rows.anchor: علم الإنسان نفسه علما وجدانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says a human's belly is filled only by dust, underscoring that acquisitiveness has no natural endpoint.
rows.anchor: ولا يملأ جوف ابن آدم إلا التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report about the last person to leave Hell says he swears not to ask for more, then requests further gifts after receiving what he sought, illustrating how satisfaction expands into further desire.
rows.anchor: كما في حديث آخر أهل النار خروجا منها يقسم لربه أنه لا يسأل غير ما طلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning also anticipates this needy community receiving the world's treasuries and becoming arrogant like earlier peoples, even while denying that danger.
rows.anchor: هذه الأمة المحتاجة ستفتح لها خزائن الأرض فيطغيها الغنى كما أطغى من قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet foretold conquest and abundant meals, his hearers said the earlier days were better because they allowed more worship; he corrected them, saying their present state was better.
rows.anchor: أنتم اليوم خير من يومئذ , فقالوا : بل يومئذ , نتفرغ لعبادة ربنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet said he feared prosperity and competition for worldly goods more than poverty, since such competition destroyed earlier peoples and could destroy his community.
rows.anchor: ما الفقر أخشى عليكم , ولكن أخسى أن يبسط عليكم الدنيا كما بسطت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return to God is unavoidable in worldly life, where no one acts except by His decree, and in the afterlife, where He judges and rewards or punishes deeds; this threatens the transgressor and humbles temporary wealth.
rows.anchor: أما في الدنيا فلا محيد عن الإقرار به , فإنه لا يقدر أحد على شيء إلا بتقديره

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim that Abū Jahl threatened to smash the Prophet's head if he saw him prostrate, but recoiled when he approached; versions describe a terrifying barrier, fire trench, wings, or a fiery camel-like figure.
rows.anchor: وأصل الحديث في صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When raʾayta is not literal sight, it means “tell me” or “inform me”; here the question presses the listener to know the forbiddance clearly.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الفعل إذا لم يكن بصريا كان بمعنى اخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yanhā depicts persistent forbidding, not a single incident.
rows.anchor: أي على سبيل التجديد والاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the worshipper a servant intensifies the condemnation: he is God's slave, and prayer is service to the Lord whose sovereignty no one can deny.
rows.anchor: قال معبرا بالعبودية منكرا للمبالغة في تقبيح النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the greatest form of worship because it joins the servant to God while entirely detaching him from creation; forbidding it denies God His due, perhaps from envy or transgression.
rows.anchor: وهي أعظم أنواع العبادة لأنها مع كونها أقرب وصلة إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode illustrates a recurring hostility in every age: people oppose the virtuous and obstruct good lest others attain distinction.
rows.anchor: من طبع أهل كل زمان عداوة أهل الفضل وصدهم عن الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question asks about the forbiddener's state, not his person, and intensifies wonder and warning about his conduct.
rows.anchor: فقال مكررا العامل زيادة في التأكيد وبيانا لأن هذا في الحقيقة أول السؤال عن الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the forbiddener is firmly on complete guidance, he should stop this worshipper from serving the acknowledged Lord only if he has a sound basis; the wording stresses his stability in that state.
rows.anchor: وعبر بأداة الاستعلاء إشارة إلى أنه في غاية الثبات والتمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining piety builds the inner self with light through guidance and then orders outward conduct; the forbiddener would be urging the worshipper to keep serving his Lord and thereby avoid divine anger.
rows.anchor: أي التي هي عماد الدين , وهي عمارة الباطن بالنور الناشئة عن الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to the first two rhetorical questions is omitted: would it not be better for him to test each matter by evidence before acting, to establish whether it is guidance and piety?
rows.anchor: فليتدبر كل أمر من أموره فلا يقدم عليه حتى يعلم بالدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the forbiddener denies that the praying servant is guided and turns away from accepting piety, the omitted answer is that such baseless denial and turning away are plainly evil.
rows.anchor: والجواب محذوف تقديره : ألم يكن ذلك التولي والتكذيب شرا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question supplies the second object of raʾayta: does the forbiddener not know that God sees, with absolute knowledge and sight of every knowable and visible thing?
rows.anchor: ذاكرا مفعول ( أرءيت ) الثاني وهو لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who sees all is able to destroy the misguiding wrongdoer and help whoever obeys Him against enemies; the rebuke uses what the opponents themselves acknowledge, exposing the contradiction in their hostility to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فهو يعلم كل معلوم ويبصر كل مبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers an ellipsis-based reading: the first pair asks about a possible righteous state and the second about a corrupt one, with the final question about God's seeing serving as the answer to both.
rows.anchor: هذا ويمكن , وهو أحسن , أن تنزل الآية على الاحتباك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, God approves and enables what is right and forbids and accounts for what is corrupt; the forbiddener should weigh conduct against rational and revealed proof.
rows.anchor: فيعلم أهي مما يرضيه ليقره عليه كما يقر سائر ما يرضيه أو يسخطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author regards the forbiddener's conduct as irrational toward himself and his fellow human beings, despite God's watching and control over him.
rows.anchor: من حالته البعيدة عن العقل مع نفسه ومع نفسه ومع أبناء جنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical ellipsis is ḥabk rather than syntactic competition: the second mention omits the state of misguidance inferable from guidance, and the first omits God's seeing, stated in the second.
rows.anchor: فحذف الكون على الضلال ثانيا لدلالة الكون على الهدى عليه أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forbiddener ignores acknowledged knowledge out of appetite and low character, so the emphatic rebuke says he has no real knowledge and cannot carry out his intended harm.
rows.anchor: أي ليس عنده علم بشيء من ذلك لسفول رتبته عن رتبة البهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure to stop is deliberate disregard and chosen blindness, not excusable heedlessness; the threat keeps the duty intact while leaving hope for repentance.
rows.anchor: إنما هو عن تهاون بالخير ورضى بالعمى والتقليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the man does not desist, God will seize him forcefully by the forelock, dragging, pulling, striking, and humiliating him; taking the most honored part of the head is especially disgraceful.
rows.anchor: لنأخذن ونقبضن قبضا وأخذا بشدة وعنف مع الجر والاجتذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite forelock identifies the known one, and the threat omits dragging him to Hell because capture in this humiliating posture already entails destruction.
rows.anchor: واستغنى بتعريف العهد عن الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forelock is described as deliberately lying and committing other sins without intent as well; this mixture reflects its owner's corrupt disposition.
rows.anchor: فهي صادر عنها الذنب من الكذب وغيره من غير تعمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the forelock itself a liar and sinner is figurative attribution to its owner and heightens the eloquence and severity of the threat.
rows.anchor: ووصفها بما هو لصاحبها على الإسناد المجازي مبالغة في تكذيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nādī is the gathering place and the people who meet there by day; the threatened man is told to summon his associates and kin to rescue him from humiliation.
rows.anchor: وأقرب من يعتز به الإنسان أهل ناديه , وهم القوم الذين يجتمعون نهارا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet identified Abū Jahl as the man who boasted, “You threaten me while I have the largest gathering in the valley.”
rows.anchor: والذي نزلت فيه هو أبو جهل , قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : أتهددني وأنا أكثر أهل الوادي ناديا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will summon the zabāniya, Hell's appointed helpers who drag offenders there; the term originally refers to guards and those who push, and describes powerful, imposing beings.
rows.anchor: أي الأعوان الموكلين بالنار ليجروه إليها , وهم في الأصل الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular zabniya is explained through the root zabn, pushing, or as a nisba form whose tāʾ replaces yāʾ.
rows.anchor: الواحد زبنية كهبرية , من الزبن وهو الدفع أو زبني على النسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Uthmānic codices omit the wāw in yadʿu; the author speculates this avoids attributing independent elevated strength to the angels, or makes their summoning certain and irresistible, or shows that the slightest call suffices.
rows.anchor: وقد اجتمعت المصاحف العثمانية على حذف الواو من هذا الفعل خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke means the man can neither summon his associates successfully nor deter the worshipper by threats, so both presumed powers are denied.
rows.anchor: أي لا يقدر على دعاء ناديه ولا ينتهي عن أذاه للمطيع بالتهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not obey the man who forbids worship; he should continue praying and humbling himself, with prostration representing both prayer and worship generally.
rows.anchor: أي دم على صلاتك وخضوعك بنفسك وجدد ذلك في كل وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration brings the servant nearest to God, so he should strive inwardly for nearness and affection through every act of worship, especially prayer.
rows.anchor: فإنه أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī reads the prayer of refuge as a spiritual ascent: first witnessing God's acts, then His attributes, then His essence, ending in loss of awareness of the self and recognition that God alone praises Himself.
rows.anchor: كما قال الإمام الغزالي في كتاب الشكر - مشاهدة أفعاله الله فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet moved through spiritual stations, treating earlier ranks as deficient by comparison; his repeated seeking forgiveness seventy times a day reflects this ascent.
rows.anchor: إنه ليغان على قلبي حتى أستغفر الله في اليوم والليلة سبعين مرة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha asked why the Prophet wept and exerted himself in prostration although his past and future sins were forgiven.
rows.anchor: ولما قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها : قد غفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet answered that he should be a grateful servant, which the author interprets as seeking further spiritual stations because gratitude brings increase.
rows.anchor: معناه : أفلا أكون طالبا للمزيد في المقامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says gratitude is the reason for increase, citing God's promise to increase those who give thanks.
rows.anchor: فإن الشكر سبب الزيادة حيث قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers seek pride, independence, and status through their community, fearing the shame of becoming followers and subordinates.
rows.anchor: وكان الكفار إنما يقصدون بأعراضهم الشماخة والأنفة والعز عن أن يكونوا أتباعا أذنابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Abraham's scroll advising the wise person to guard the tongue, understand the times, and attend to his own affairs.
rows.anchor: ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of al-Qadr is to detail the divine command implied by the purpose of Iqraʾ; its name comes from the night being honored by the Qur'an revealed in it, treating the effect as the cause.
rows.anchor: مقصودها تفصيل الأمر الذي هو أحد قسمي ما ضمنه مقصود ' اقرأ '

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's name supports the view that times are honored because of what occurs in them, as with the day on which the verse completing the religion was revealed.
rows.anchor: وهو دليل لمن يقول باعتبار تفضيل الأوقات لأجل ما كان فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUmar told the Jewish questioner that the day of the verse's revelation became two festivals for Muslims: because it was both ʿArafa and Friday.
rows.anchor: وأفرده الفاروق عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه على ذلك وأعلمه أنه صار لنا عيدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala praises God's majesty, universal mercy, and special completion of blessings for the people of monotheism.
rows.anchor: الذي خص أهل التوحيد بإتمام النعمة فاختصت بهم جناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qadr details one of the two parts of the command encapsulated in Iqraʾ; the night is honored through the Qur'an, so its name uses the effect to name its cause.
rows.anchor: مقصودها تفصيل الأمر الذي هو أحد قسمي ما ضمنه مقصود ' اقرأ '

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah supports honoring times for the events occurring in them, as with the day the completion-of-religion verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وهو دليل لمن يقول باعتبار تفضيل الأوقات لأجل ما كان فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUmar explained that Muslims gained two festivals on that day, since it was both the day of ʿArafa and Friday.
rows.anchor: وأعلمه أنه صار لنا عيدين : عيدا من جهة كونه يوم عرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening praises God's exalted majesty, universal mercy, and special completion of blessings for monotheists.
rows.anchor: الذي خص أهل التوحيد بإتمام النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “it” refers to the Qur'an, already present in the heart and context through the preceding command to read and the closing command to pray; reciting Qur'an in prayer is the route to nearness.
rows.anchor: ذكر إنزاله مستحضرا في كل قلب , كان ذلك مغنيا عن إعادته بصريح اسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the Qur'an unnamed magnifies it, as if nothing else was sent down that requires explicit mention; God's own act of sending and the majestic plural further exalt it.
rows.anchor: فكان إضماره أدل على العظمة الباهرة من إظهاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entire Qur'an descended from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven's Bayt al-ʿIzza in the order now agreed by the protected Muslim community.
rows.anchor: أي هذا الذكر كله من اللوح المحفوظ إلى بيت العزة من السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first revelation was the opening five verses, sent to Muhammad while he was near Mount Ḥirāʾ during the sacred month; later passages descended over twenty-three years according to events.
rows.anchor: وأول ما أنزل منه صدرها إلى خمس آيات منها آخرها ( ما لم يعلم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whenever a passage descended, God commanded the Prophet where to place it in its surah until the Qur'an reached its present arrangement.
rows.anchor: وكلما نزل منه نجم يأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بترتيبه في سورته عن أمر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laylat al-Qadr has immense rank and honor, and deeds performed in it likewise have great worth.
rows.anchor: أي الليلة التي لها قدر عظيم وشرف كبير , والأعمال فيها ذات قدر وشرف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the surah identifies when the previously commanded reading was revealed; the Book is the path to God, and the hidden night should prompt supplication, hope, and effort, like the concealed Friday hour and middle prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : ورد تعريفا بإنزال ماتقدم الأمر بقراءته

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says that explaining the night’s great rank also explains the Qur'an's exalted status and completes the connection to the preceding surah.
rows.anchor: وكان في التعريف بعظيم قدر هذه الليلة التعريف بجلالة المنزل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “what is the Night of Decree?” signals that even the Prophet's extensive knowledge cannot reach the full extent of its merit.
rows.anchor: لم تبلغ درايتك وأنت أعلم الناس غاية فضلها ومنتهى علي قدرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is better than a thousand months, meaning either the night itself is better than months without it or worship on it surpasses worship in a thousand months lacking it—eighty-three years and four months.
rows.anchor: أي خالية عنها أو العمل فيها خير من العمل في ألف شهر ليس فيها ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: Some say the thousand months correspond to the duration of Umayyad rule.
rows.anchor: قالوا : وهي مدة ملك بني أمية سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Qadr may denote the night’s honor or the decree of annual destinies copied from the Mother of the Book; the latter reading links it to Sūrat al-Dukhān.
rows.anchor: أو أنه يفصل فيها من أم الكتاب مقادير الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thousand may be a rhetorical maximum, but it may also recall a believer from the Children of Israel who fought for a thousand months, prompting God to give this community a night better than that.
rows.anchor: أو لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر شخصا من مؤمني بني إسرائيل لبس السلاح مجاهدا في سبيل الله ألف شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority place the hidden night in Ramadan's final ten nights, based on sound reports; concealment encourages seeking it, like the Friday response hour, middle prayer, God's greatest name, approval, anger, and the Hour.
rows.anchor: وأبهمها في العشر الأخير من شهر رمضان في قول الجمهور على ما صح من الأحاديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hiding a precious reward ensures people strive for it and appreciate it; the thirty-word surah may indicate the twenty-seventh night, matching the word “hiya,” as Abū Bakr al-Warrāq transmitted.
rows.anchor: لكن جعل السورة ثلاثين كلمة سواء يرجح أنهم السابعة والعشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels descend swiftly and in succession; al-Rūḥ may be Gabriel, the most honored angels, a being greater than angels, or a spiritual affair that consoles the knowers.
rows.anchor: أي جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام , خصه بيانا لفضله أو هو مع أشراف الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their descent occurs by their Lord's permission, knowledge, and enabling, and may be to earth, the lowest heaven, or near believers.
rows.anchor: أي بعلم المحسن إليهم المربي لهم وتمكينه , وتنزلهم إلى الأرض أو السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They descend concerning every universal matter whose details God has decreed for the coming year, or because He determines all that will occur; calling things “affairs” shows angels act only on His command.
rows.anchor: الأمور الكلية التي يفرقون فيها بإذن الله تفاصيل الأمور التي يريدها سبحانه في ذلك العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is wholly peace, goodness, and blessing without evil until dawn; the author links this to al-Kisāʾī's kasra reading of maṭlaʿ.
rows.anchor: لا يكون فيه شر كما في غير ليلتها , فلا تطلع الشمس في صبيحتها بين قرني الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using ḥattā rather than ilā means the dawn's rising time and place share the night's peaceful ruling.
rows.anchor: واخير التعبير ب ( حتى ) دون ( إلى ) ليفهم أن لما بعدها حكم ما قبلها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Gabriel descends with a band of angels carrying a green banner, plants it above the Kaʿba, then the angels greet every person praying, sitting, remembering God, bowing, or prostrating until dawn.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام ينزل ليلة القدر في كوكبة من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's grandeur should move readers to devote themselves to the Qur'an and recite it properly, trusting against Judgment's terror; honoring the night means seeking it throughout the year, Ramadan, or at least the final ten nights.
rows.anchor: فمن تأمل هذه السورة علم منه ما للقرآن من العظمة فأقبل عليه بكليته يتلوه حق تلاوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking the night and multiplying good deeds may let believers surpass even a thousand years of earlier worship, and the surah's end returns coherently to its beginning because Qur'an's descent is the night's greatest peace.
rows.anchor: ورجوع آخرها بكون هذا التنزل في ليلة القدر على أولها في غاية الوضوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's thirty words may allude to the thirty-year caliphate after the Prophet, ending when al-Ḥasan yielded authority to Muʿāwiya in Rabīʿ I 41 AH; the author analogizes that era to the Night of Decree among ordinary nights.
rows.anchor: إن خلافة النبوة التي هي ثلاثون سنة بعد موت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: The cited Rabbanis define alif as the encompassing supreme who is absent from its station yet present in being; the author likens Abū Bakr to this, spiritually absent from people and present with God.
rows.anchor: قالوا : هو اسم للقائم المحيط الأعلى الغائب عن مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāʾ represents ʿUthmān and his original innate purity, which the author says was marred by kindness to relatives and led to grave troubles.
rows.anchor: والفاء لعثمان رضي الله تعالى عنه وهو إشارة لبدء خلوص منته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jīm represents ʿAlī and gathering: he restored some unity after ʿUthmān's martyrdom, though strife prevented full resolution.
rows.anchor: وهو إشارة إلى الجمع , والإجمال الذي يحصل عنده عنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's letter symbolism associates rāʾ with al-Ḥasan's nurturing role; he surrendered authority to Muʿāwiya to prevent Muslims from being killed.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فعل رضي الله عنه لما رأى الملك يهلك بقتل المسلمين رباه بنزوله عن الأمر لمعاوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bayyina announces the upright Book's high rank and great effects: it guides some to Paradise but brings others to Hell, dividing people into the blessed and wretched.
rows.anchor: أنه كما أنه لقوم نور وهدى فهو لآخرين وقر وعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its names, “Those who disbelieved” and “Those who were not to desist,” indicate the split between the two groups when the verses are considered.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك دل كل من اسمائها ' الذين كفروا ' ' والمنفكين ' بتأمل الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening basmala describes God's absolute elevation and will, His universal gifts of creation and clarification, and His special gift of righteous deeds that bring salvation and felicity.
rows.anchor: الذي له العلو المطلق فلا يخرج شيء عن مراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the hidden descent and identity of the blessed night last until dawn, people of every religion normally change only through a proof clearer than dawn; the Qur'an and its messenger are that decisive proof.
rows.anchor: لم يصح في العادة الجارية على حكمة الأسباب في دار الأسباب أن يتحولوا عما هم فيه إلا بسبب عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They were not to desist” spans past, present, and future as a settled disposition, unlike the earlier habit of changing among disbelief and innovation without remaining firm.
rows.anchor: في مطلق الزمان الماضي والحال والاستقبال كونا هو كالجبلة والطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses the Israelites repeatedly became blind and deaf and repented, then relapsed; the verse describing this is evidence for their instability.
rows.anchor: كما دل على بعض ذلك قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab polytheists shifted among worshipping idols, angels, and jinn rather than holding one belief; after the proof of Islam, converts abandoned pre-Islamic practices such as gambling and the customs of sāʾiba.
rows.anchor: وتارة يبعدون الأصنام , وتارة الملائكة , وأخرى الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book are mentioned first because they knew revelation and bore greater responsibility; they altered and distorted their originally true religion, so God replaced their legal details while preserving agreement on fundamentals.
rows.anchor: بدأ بقوله : { من أهل الكتاب } أي من اليهود والنصارى الذين كان أصل دينهم حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists worshipped idols, fire, the sun, and similar things; the author describes them as wholly detached from their former religion and invokes their prior expectation of a coming messenger.
rows.anchor: أي بعبادة الأصنام والنار والشمس ونحو ذلك
